<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par128 />genitive {{GHGheb|text=הֲלוּמֵי יַ֫יִן}} then depends, in reality explains nothing; the text is almost certainly corrupt. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁנֵה}} would be expected; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבְּרִית}} is a later addition; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=מָשׂוֹשׂ}}), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=22}} ({{GHGheb|text=שֵׂעָר}}), the absolute for the construct state probably rests only on the authority of the Masoretes. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=25}} ff. the text is obviously in confusion. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=32}} (cf. 6:24) {{GHGheb|text=כְּעָפְרָה}} should come either after {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקָּבֵר}} or at the end of the verse, unless, with Moore, we omit {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִי הָֽע׳}} as a gloss (from 6:24); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=משֶׁה}} is probably a gloss on {{GHGheb|text=יְמֵי־עוֹלָם}} which has crept into the text; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לְאִישׁ־בּ֫שֶׁת}}, according to the LXX, has dropped out before {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=רָעוֹת}} is to be omitted with the LXX; if originally in the text, it could only be genitive (= ''all abominations of evils''), not an adjective; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=6}} the text is altogether uncertain (the LXX read {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹקְשֵׁי}} for {{GHGheb|text=מְבַקְשֵׁי}}); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=13}} the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (after a {{GHGheb|text=ל}}) has dropped out before {{GHGheb|text=מְלֶאכֶת}} (cf. 12:25).—Elsewhere ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=5}}) the supposed genitives are to be taken rather as words of nearer definition standing in apposition, i.e. ''with high walls, gates, and bars''. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=ירושלים}} is either in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=העם הזה}} or is better (since not in the LXX) omitted as a gloss.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|d}}
(''b'') Genitives after a noun with a suffix (where the suffix prevents the direct government by the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}). Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=27|verse=3}}, 5, 6, where {{GHGheb|text=הַזָּכָר}} after {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְכְּךָ}}<ref>Halévy, ''J. A.'' xiv. 548, removes the difficulty by pointing {{GHGheb|text=עַרְכֹּךְ}}.</ref> might be taken, contrary to the accents, as subject of the following clause; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=15}}, 25 the suffix may refer to Moses. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=מִדּוֹ בַד|translate=his garment}}, namely the garment ''of linen'', unless simply in apposition, cf. {{GHGpar|131|d}} (or read {{GHGheb|text=מִדֵּי}}?); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=42}}, where {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי יַֽעֲקֹב וגו׳}} could at most be explained as an ellipse for {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי בְרִית יַֽעֲקֹב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|125|h}} (probably, however, it is a case of dittography of the {{GHGheb|text=י}}, which was repeated also before {{GHGheb|text=אברהם}}; so Valeton, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} xii. 3); equally strange is {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי הַיּוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=20}}, &c. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=אִם יִֽהְיֶה נְבִֽיאֲכֶם יְהֹוָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=12|verse=6}} could not possibly mean ''if your prophet be a prophet of the Lord''; the text is manifestly corrupt (probably {{GHGheb|text=נְבִֽיאֲךָ מִיַּהְוֶה}} is to be read, with Marti). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּסְאֲךָ אֱלֹהִים}} (usually explained as ''thy divine throne''), {{GHGheb|text=אלהים}} is most probably a later addition [another suggestion is to read {{GHGheb|text=כֵאלֹהִים|translate=like God}}(''’s throne''): cf. {{GHGpar|141|d}}, note]. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=52|verse=20}} two readings are probably combined, {{GHGheb|text=לִנְחֻשְׁתָּם}} without any addition, and {{GHGheb|text=לִנְח֫שֶׁת בָּל־הַכֵּלִיס}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם}} is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי}}. On {{GHGheb|text=דַּרְכֵּךְ זִמָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=27}}, cf. {{GHGpar|131|r}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|e}}
(''c'') The interposition of a word is assumed between {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} (''the whole''; cf. {{GHGpar|127|b}}) and the genitive governed by it in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=עוֹד}}), and, if the text is correct, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hos|chapter=14|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=תִּשָּׂא}}). In reality, however, in all three places the genitive relation is destroyed by the transposition of the words (instead of {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד כָּל־}}, &c.), and {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} is rather to be taken adverbially (equivalent to ''wholly''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=9}} ''because my life is yet wholly in me'', i.e. my whole life; cf. Philippi, ''Stat. Constr.'', p. 10.—On the instances in which the original construct state {{GHGheb|text=אֵין|translate=non-existence}} is used without a following genitive, see the negative sentences, {{GHGpar|152|o}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|f}}
